content.title: How Casualty's harrowing death episode sets up 5 major new stories
content.text: Casualty spoilers followThe conclusion of Casualty’s latest boxset ‘Learning Curve’ was incredibly dramatic, with a tragic death confirmed in an ominous flashforward funeral scene. With Faith Dean experiencing serious complications after her premature labour, and Kim Chang found unconscious by Matty Linlaker, both of their lives were on the line.But sadly, it was Kim who passed away, suffering multi-organ failure as a result of her eating disorder.BBC Related: Best streaming servicesIt was a truly devastating episode, as the ED came together to say goodbye to one of their own. Rising star Jasmine Bayes delivered a brilliant, layered performance as Kim over just a few short months, while her character's story showed how destructive eating disorders can be, especially when they are kept hidden. Kim’s death was powerful in its own right, but as we head into the next boxset – titled ‘Lethal Legacy’ – next week, this finale episode also sets up some huge new stories for the surviving characters in Holby.What to Read Next 1. Stevie's guiltBBCAdvertisement - Continue Reading BelowAs Kim’s mentor, Stevie was often incredibly tough on her young resident during her rotation at Holby. She wanted Kim to grow a thicker skin and have more confidence in her decision-making – but while Kim was clearly a talented doctor, her eating disorder began to impact her health, which led to her making mistakes at work.Viewers who know and love Stevie were aware that she only ever wanted to make Kim a better doctor and to prepare her for life in the ED, but she only found out about her mentee’s illness shortly before her death. When Matty handed her Kim’s journal, she was devastated to realise that her words had left scars and exacerbated the feelings of failure that Kim’s dad said had triggered her eating disorder.At the funeral, Stevie said: "I know Kim would have made a brilliant doctor. The bit I didn’t know was that she wouldn’t get to be around to hear me say that." While Stevie is in no way responsible for Kim’s death, it is likely that she will blame herself for what happened – and these feelings of guilt will stick with her in the next boxset.2. Matty's futureBBCWhen Kim quit the rotation in A&E, Flynn offered Matty the clinical fellowship that was up for grabs for one of the residents. Matty was cynical and questioned whether he’d only earned the fellowship by being the last man standing. But Kim’s death put things into perspective, and outside the church Matty declared that he was going to do the fellowship for both of them.However, the loss of his colleague and friend will also have a huge effect on Matty. He was the only member of the team who knew about Kim’s eating disorder and urged her to seek support on multiple occasions. While he did everything he could, he is no doubt going to blame himself for not being able to save her.As he begins the next chapter of his career in Holby, in the next boxset Matty’s grief will push him towards a very unexpected source of comfort…3. Dylan's second chanceBBCAdvertisement - Continue Reading BelowAfter finding out that Matty would be sticking around for a while in the ED, Dylan took the opportunity to connect with his secret son. While Matty previously rejected him, at Kim’s funeral Dylan suggested that they should try and explore some sort of relationship, and Matty agreed.But Matty made it clear that if they were going to spend more time together, his mum – and Dylan’s former flame Sarah – would want to see him. Dylan looked rather nervous about the idea of reuniting with a face from his past, but viewers can look forward to meeting Sarah for the first time as Matty and Dylan finally start getting to know each other properly.4. Faith and Iain's reunionBBCThis final episode was touch and go for Faith, who gave birth to her baby then had to undergo life-saving surgery in the aftermath. During this time, things were still tricky with Iain, and the pair were arguing about joint custody arrangements when Faith went into labour unexpectedly.When Faith arrived at hospital, Iain told Stevie that "if you have to save one, save her". Faith overheard this and assumed that he was talking about the baby, but Iain later said that actually he meant her. The pair were still at odds after the birth, but when Faith’s condition deteriorated again, Iain realised that he had been a fool to ever let her go.At the end of the episode, after Faith pulled through, she and Iain got to spend time with their baby together, who they decided to name Pearl. The separated couple shared a kiss and looked more united than ever. Has Pearl’s arrival brought Faith and Iain back together, or could there be some more rocky times ahead?5. Rash's new roleBBCIt’s been a quiet time for Rash on screen recently, but we know that he is currently on the CESR pathway, the journey towards becoming a consultant – and the next stage of this pathway has now been confirmed. Outside the church at Kim’s funeral, Iain was talking to Flynn and Rash about the brilliance of the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) and Rash explained that he was about to start a rotation in that department.Rash’s experience in NICU will be documented in the next boxset, and he could be involved with the care of Iain and Faith’s baby, who remains in the unit for now. How will Rash cope with this new challenge?The next Casualty boxset, ‘Lethal Legacy’, will kick off next Saturday (25 April), and you can check out our round-up of all the biggest moments from the dramatic first episode on Tuesday.Beat is a charity which raises awareness and understanding of eating disorders, and supports those affected by them. It has a one-to-one secure messaging service, and details of its phone helplines can be found here.Casualty airs on Saturday nights on BBC One and now streams first on BBC iPlayer, where episodes are released at 6am on the day of transmission.Read more Casualty spoilers on our dedicated homepage
